To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dissolution behaviour of the ILs is primarily governed by the interactions between anion of the ionic liquid and the hydroxyl protons of cellulose and xylan.
the anions of ionic liquids play a significant role in the dissolution of celluloses and hemicellloses in ionic liquids.
the anion of IL plays an important role in the solubility of cellulose and xylans, which is confirmed by both quantum chemical and experimental results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the interaction mechanism of cellulose/hemcellulose with ILs.
the development of new and efficient ionic liquid for the dissolution of lignocellulosic biomass.
the development of new ILs for the dissolution of lignocellulosic biomass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acetate [OAC] anion and [EMIM]cation are the best ILs for the dissolution of both cellulose and hycellulose.
the dissolution process of cellulose/hemi-cellulose in IL is primarily governed by hydrogen bond interactions between the anion of IL and cellulose/hemicelullose.
the dissolution of celluloses and hemicellulos in ionic liquids is primarily determined by the anion of IL and the cation of the IL has a minor contribution in the dissolution process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present study has provided a detailed understanding of the solvation process of cellulose and its derivatives in ILs and the results would help in the development of new ILs for the dissolution of biomass in the near future.
the dissolution of cellululose and hemicelulose in IL is primarily dependent on the hydrogen bonds between the anion of IL and the hydroxyl group of the cellulose and hemeclulose molecules.
the COSMO RS model can predict the dissolution behaviour of biomass in ILs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dissolution of biomass in ILs can be explained by the quantum chemical and COSMO RS calculations.
the quantum chemical and molecular dynamics simulations can be used as a tool to screen the potential ILs for the dissolution of lignocellulosic biomass.
the COSMORS model is a good tool to predict the activity coefficients of ILs and to screen out the best ILs for the dissolution of biomass.
